content: Tenapanor is indicated for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults. The recommended dosage is 50 mg taken orally twice daily, immediately before breakfast and dinner. It is also indicated for reducing serum phosphorus levels in adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD) on dialysis, as an add-on therapy for patients who have an inadequate response to phosphate binders or are intolerant to any dose of phosphate binder therapy. For this indication, the recommended dosage is 30 mg taken orally twice daily, immediately before breakfast and dinner. Serum phosphorus levels should be monitored, and the dosage adjusted as needed to manage gastrointestinal tolerability. No dose adjustments are required for patients with renal or hepatic impairment. The safety and efficacy of tenapanor have not been established in patients under 18 years of age. It is contraindicated in children under 6 years of age due to the risk of severe dehydration, as observed in studies with young juvenile rats. Use should also be avoided in children aged 6 to less than 12 years for the same reason. Additionally, tenapanor is contraindicated in patients with known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction. If severe diarrhea occurs, dosing should be suspended, and the patient should be rehydrated. Tenapanor is minimally absorbed systemically, with plasma concentrations below the limit of quantification. There is no available data on the presence of tenapanor in human or animal milk, its effects on milk production, or its effects on breastfed infants. This includes drugs such as atorvastatin, bosentan, conjugated estrogens, enalapril, fexofenadine, fluvastatin, glyburide, pravastatin, and rosuvastatin. For these drugs, caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. Sodium polystyrene sulfonate may decrease the level or effect of tenapanor by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. When both agents are administered orally, therapy should be modified, and administration should be separated by at least three hours. Tenapanor should be stored at 68–77°F (20–25°C), with excursions permitted to 59–86°F (15–30°C). It should be kept in its tightly closed original container, protected from moisture, and the desiccant should not be removed. The medication should not be subdivided or repackaged. This information is provided for general educational purposes. Individual treatment plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider.
